property_tax_california.value: Within 3 years of transfer, or before any transfer to a third party
$1,044,586 for transfers 2/16/2025 - 2/15/2027; adjusted every two years using the FHFA House Price Index for California
property_tax_california.note: Projections after 2027 assume the add-on grows with inflation (assumption).

property_tax_california.value: If market value <= factored base-year value + add-on, the base-year value is kept. If market value is higher, the excess over (base-year value + add-on) is added to the base-year value; so taxable value = market value - add-on. BOE example (FAQ 6): base-year value $300,000, market value $1,500,000 -> excluded $1,300,000; $200,000 added -> adjusted base-year value $500,000.
property_tax_california.note: Read directly from BOE FAQ 6 (verified). The earlier project note was checked against this text.

property_tax_california.value: Only the unit occupied as the principal residence qualifies; other units are reassessed to full cash value
property_tax_california.note: Relevant to Property B (3 units) if it were ever inherited.

property_tax_california.value: Trust is looked through; the rules apply to the beneficiary's occupancy, not the vehicle

If the transferee stops occupying the home, the exclusion ends and the home is reassessed as of the lien date after the move-out. The new taxable value is the market value on the date of inheritance, adjusted each year by the inflation factor (BOE FAQ 3). A different eligible transferee occupying within one year can keep the exclusion.
